title: introduce lightweight sampled-profile harness and compact changelog seed
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: onboarding new models currently requires a manual, full-profile pass that is slow and expensive for initial acceptance. This PR adds a lightweight, sampled profiling harness that seeds a compact performance profile and a small 'changelog seed' artifact that the release assembler can consume to generate early release notes and regression hints. The goal is to make model triage fast: produce an initial cost/latency estimate and highlight obvious compatibility or perf regressions before running the full calibration pipeline.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a `profile-seed` runner that performs deterministic, sampled inference traces against a curated prompt corpus and quantization/config variants; it produces a compact profile (latency percentiles, sample token counts, KV-warmup guidance) and a machine-readable changelog seed that records observed diffs between current and baseline variants. Also wires a post-merge CI job that uploads the seed artifact to the release pipeline so downstream assemblers can include notes and candidate regression warnings.

Checklist: [x] sampled profiling harness (registry/onboard/seed_profiler.py) [x] CI job + k8s job manifest (ci/profilers/profile-seed-job.yaml) [x] compact seed schema and serializer (registry/schema/profile_seed_schema.yaml) [x] small CLI shim to run locally (scripts/run_profile_seed.sh) [x] unit and smoke integration tests (tests/test_seed_profiler.py) [x] docs: onboarding quickstart and privacy notes (docs/onboarding/quickstart-profiling.md)

Design notes: The harness samples workloads instead of exhaustive runs to keep runtime under 10 minutes on a small GPU. Sampling uses stratified prompts drawn from the model's prerecorded prompt-corpus manifest (if available) with a configurable deterministic RNG seed to make results repeatable. For latency estimation we warm the KV cache with a single prefix pass per prompt group then measure steady-state P50/P95/P99 across N inferences. Cost estimates are derived from tokenization + measured per-token latency and multiplied against measured throughput; this intentionally errs on the conservative side. The changelog seed contains per-variant bulletized findings (e.g. "+12ms P95 vs baseline", "increased tokenizer OOV ratio: 0.4%") and a short machine-check field for likely breakages (tokenization drift, output shape mismatch) so the release assembler can highlight actionable items.

Privacy/security: prompt corpus sampling uses only datasets flagged as "public" or "scrubbed" per registry metadata; if no approved corpus exists the run defaults to synthetic prompts generated from model-spec templates. No raw prompts are uploaded as part of the seed artifact; only hashed prompt identifiers and aggregate stats are stored. We added a short policy note in docs/onboarding/quickstart-profiling.md.

Backward compatibility: The compact seed uses a forward-compatible schema (profile_seed_schema.yaml). The release assembler will ignore unknown fields. No registry schema changes required for existing profiles.

Testing: Unit tests cover serializer roundtrip, deterministic sampling, and the cost estimator. Integration smoke runs the harness against a small toy model in CI; the smoke job was flaky initially because of different tokenizer versions in the CI image — fixed by pinning tokenizer package in the CI job manifest.

Follow-ups: 1) add expansion to run a small battery of quantized variants automatically (ENG-2240 follow-up), 2) integrate with model-onboard UI to show the seed summary in the first-stage review panel, 3) schedule nightly re-seeds for active variants to detect regressions early.

Related: Linear ENG-2154, ENG-2240; SUP-982 (support case that motivated faster triage).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice direction. Two questions: how do we ensure sample representativeness across long-tail prompts? Please document the sampling heuristics and add a knob for stratified oversampling of rare buckets.
Aisha Kapoor: answered — added stratified sampling logic and a --sample-weight config option, documented heuristics in quickstart-profiling.md.
Mariana Ortiz: Concerned about leakage — can we avoid storing raw prompts in artifacts? Also CI flaked on tokenizer mismatch earlier.
Aisha Kapoor: confirmed — artifacts only contain hashed prompt ids and aggregated stats; fixed CI by pinning tokenizer version in the CI manifest; added policy note to docs.
Devon Patel: Can the changelog seed accidentally mark false positives for regressions when perf variance is high? Suggest a simple baseline-stability check or sig-test.

Aisha Kapoor: implemented a basic bootstrap-based stability gate that marks a finding as "likely" only if delta exceeds 2x sample stddev; otherwise flags as "noisy" and includes raw stats for later evaluation.
Mariana Ortiz: Approved after changes — left an approval review.
Liam Chen: LGTM. Squash-merge when CI passes.
ci_checks: integration-smoke: pass (profile-runner smoke against toy model)
e2e: skipped (not required for seed harness)
release_notes: Adds a lightweight sampled profiling harness and compact changelog seed artifact. Seeds initial performance profiles for faster onboarding and automatic hints for potential regressions. No breaking changes.
notes: Post-merge: A post-merge workflow uploads the seed artifact to the release assembler S3 prefix. Ops notified to add the profile-runner image to the registry image allowlist for Dedicated deployments.
incident_tie_in: This PR was prompted by SUP-982 where a customer needed quicker triage for a failing model upgrade; the seed artifact would have surfaced a tokenizer drift earlier.
manual_steps: To run locally: scripts/run_profile_seed.sh --model <model-id> --manifest path/to/manifest.yaml --out seed.json ; review seed.json with scripts/assemble_changelog_seed.sh to generate human notes.
